sections.mechanism_or_content: Defines the unknown-bias coin/stopping-time model, fast exponential tails, and the analytic characterization goal.
Derives nested lower/upper Bernstein polynomials from finite input words, proves consistency, and constructs a factory whose exact tail equals the envelope gap.
Builds a doubling algorithm for a clipped linear function and bounds its tail using binomial/hypergeometric concentration.
Closure constructions and positive power-series operations yield fast algorithms on specified domains.
Proves analyticity necessity and derives smoothness from finite moments only under uniform moment-tail decay; finite expectation has a separate compact-uniform Lipschitz result.
Approximates the doubling step for algorithmic constructions; does not change the main characterization.
Gives a terminating construction using a positive-polynomial representation.
Lists unresolved rate/moment questions and bibliographic sources.
States the paired p-coin/fair-coin input-stage model, stopping rule, rate definition and smoothness goal; rendered p.2 confirms Δ_n(x)=max{sqrt(x(1−x)/n),1/n}.

Defines Bernstein-positive order and consistent envelope sequences; distinguishes pure p-only integer condition (ii) from the fair-coin-assisted dyadic-multiple condition (ii′), and states Theorem 8 for noninteger α.
Uses Bernstein-positive derivative inequalities on dyadic increments, splits sums at the scale |x−y|, and proves the C^α necessity; integer case gives only Zygmund necessity.
Polynomial-reproducing corrected Bernstein operators, coefficient recurrences, derivative bounds, and boundary-sensitive simultaneous approximation lemmas.
Builds geometric-degree approximants inductively, controls derivatives/norms/coefficients, then adds a positive Bernstein majorant and checks coefficient monotonicity to obtain the tail gap.
Constructs a counterexample to a claimed converse from positive Bernstein approximation alone, using zero-free Taylor polynomials, Gaussian convolution and Poisson summation.
Defines the integer-order generalized Lipschitz/Zygmund class, states a conjectural integer-order sufficiency, and poses finite-α-moment classification as an open problem.
Lists approximation, Bernoulli-factory and probability sources cited in the paper.
